purpose: Standards-conforming DTMF test corpus for phone-channel-dtmf-receiver: clean keys, Q.24 stress cases with declared expected outcomes, deterministic noise, and a phone-band channel.
generation: python3 generate.py — pure stdlib, fixed noise seed 0x6D2B79F5; the corpus is exactly reproducible byte-for-byte.
spec_basis: ITU-T Q.23 (11/1988): low group 697/770/852/941 Hz, high group 1209/1336/1477/1633 Hz, +/-1.8% sending tolerance. Q.24 receiver categories (AT&T annex values): operate at <=1.5% offset, not operate at >=3.5%; twist tolerance about -8..+4 dB; accept >=40 ms, reject <23 ms. See research/texts/itu-dtmf-records.txt.

contents.content: All 16 keys in Q.23 keypad order (123A456B789C*0#D), 100 ms tone + 100 ms pause.
Sixteen single-key clips (star/hash spelled out), 50 ms silence padding.
Key 5 with both tones +1.5% off nominal: a conforming receiver must still decode 5.
+3.5% offset: a conforming receiver must NOT decode.
High tone +4 dB relative to low: twist acceptance boundary.
25 ms burst: below the rejection threshold; must not register.
45 ms burst: above the 40 ms acceptance duration; must register.
Full sequence in deterministic additive noise at 30 and 15 dB SNR.
Full sequence through the 300-3400 Hz phone-band FIR (101-tap Hamming windowed sinc).
Channel plus 15 dB SNR noise: the hardest supplied case.
The channel impulse response (n, h), so receiver analysis can account for channel gain and delay explicitly.

note: Synthetic by design: the lesson's receiver must justify thresholds against declared Q.24 categories, which requires known ground truth per clip. Learner-recorded real tones remain a suggested extension in the lesson; this corpus provides the reproducible baseline.
